title: {{NAME}} and the Three Crowns
moral: True authority comes from earning trust, not from wearing a title.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a forest-green and gold hero coat over dark trousers, gold-buckled boots, and a short green cape — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
Three forces governed the kingdom of Halcyon: Princess Maeve (royal authority), the Fairy High Council (magical authority), and the Hero Guild (protective authority).

They had not spoken directly for forty years.

Each believed the others held too much power.

The result: a kingdom that worked in separate parts and barely at all as a whole.

{{NAME}} was hired as the kingdom's first Liaison Officer, a title so new nobody knew what it meant.

"It means," he said carefully, "that I talk to all three of you and none of you have to talk directly to each other until you want to."

pages.content:
The first six months: meetings. {{NAME}} in three offices, carrying what each side needed the others to know, carefully phrased, never distorted.

He developed a skill: finding the shared interest under the stated position.

Princess Maeve wanted stability. The Fairy Council wanted their settlements protected. The Hero Guild wanted clear operational boundaries.

All three were the same thing, he realised: they all wanted to know their domain was safe.

He wrote this down and presented it to all three simultaneously.

Three separate sessions. Same document. Same words.

pages.content:
The first direct meeting of all three powers in forty years was low-key by design.

{{NAME}} booked the smallest conference room in the neutral council building.

Princess Maeve arrived first. The head fairy arrived second (on a cloud of personal transportation). The guild commander arrived third.

They sat at a round table with no head.

{{NAME}} sat in the corner with a notepad and didn't speak for the first twenty minutes.

Then he said: "You all said something similar to me. I thought you should hear it from each other."

pages.content:
The meeting lasted three hours.

By the end, there was one joint statement and three separate commitments.

The joint statement: the kingdom's authority is shared and mutual.

It had taken forty years.

On the way out, Princess Maeve stopped beside {{NAME}}.

"You never claimed credit in there," she said.

"I didn't do it," said {{NAME}}. "You three did. I just kept the path open until you were ready to walk down it."

pages.content:
He walked home through the kingdom as evening came.

Three powers. Forty years of silence. Three hours of conversation.

He had been a liaison officer for six months and was eleven years old.

In bed, he thought about the round table with no head.

That had been the key. Nobody's seat was more important. The table arranged the conversation before anyone said a word.

He fell asleep thinking about tables.
